content: Zanamivir is a medication used to treat symptoms caused by the influenza virus (flu) if symptoms have been present for two days or less. It is also used to prevent the flu in individuals who have been exposed to someone with the flu, such as a sick household member, or during a community flu outbreak. This medication works by inhibiting the growth of the flu virus. Dosage and Administration: 1. For flu treatment: Inhale the medication through the mouth as directed by your doctor, typically two inhalations (one blister per inhalation) twice daily, approximately 12 hours apart, for five days. 2. For flu prevention: Inhale the medication through the mouth as directed by your doctor, typically two inhalations (one blister per inhalation) once daily. 3. Use the Diskhaler device to administer the medication. Before use, ensure the mouthpiece is clean and free of particles. Load the medication disk into the Diskhaler, puncture one blister, and keep the device level to prevent spillage. Exhale fully, place the mouthpiece in your mouth, and inhale deeply to draw the medication into your lungs. Hold your breath for a few seconds. For additional doses, advance to the next blister and repeat the process. Important Usage Instructions: Start zanamivir as soon as possible after symptom onset or exposure for maximum effectiveness. Continue using the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve. If you have breathing problems (e.g., asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), use your bronchodilator medication (e.g., albuterol) before using zanamivir. Side Effects: Common side effects include dizziness, increased coughing, headache, throat or tonsil pain, and nausea. Rarely, serious breathing problems such as wheezing or shortness of breath may occur, which can be fatal in some cases. If these occur, stop using zanamivir and seek immediate medical attention. Allergic reactions, including oropharyngeal edema, rash, or anaphylaxis, are rare but possible. Discontinue use and seek medical care if an allergic reaction is suspected. Rarely, zanamivir or the flu itself may cause serious mental or mood changes, such as confusion, agitation, hallucinations, or abnormal behavior, particularly in children. Precautions: Inform your doctor if you are allergic to zanamivir or any of its ingredients (e.g., lactose, milk proteins). Avoid using this medication if you have severe lung or breathing problems unless directed by your doctor. Zanamivir may cause dizziness; avoid driving or operating machinery until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcohol and marijuana use, as these can exacerbate dizziness. During pregnancy, use this medication only if clearly needed. There is no definitive evidence of harm to the fetus, but data is limited. Discuss risks and benefits with your doctor. It is unknown if zanamivir passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Inform your doctor of all medications and supplements you are taking, as drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of zanamivir or increase the risk of side effects. If you have received a nasal flu vaccine within the past two weeks, inform your doctor, as zanamivir may interfere with the vaccine's effectiveness. Overdose: In case of overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. Storage: Store at room temperature in a dry place. Do not puncture the foil blister until ready to use. Avoid storing in the bathroom. Properly discard expired or unused medication. Additional Information: Zanamivir is not a substitute for the flu vaccine. Effectiveness is highest when used within 24–48 hours of symptom onset. Safety and efficacy in patients with high-risk underlying medical conditions have not been established. Do not attempt to create an extemporaneous solution for nebulization or mechanical ventilation, as this can lead to fatal complications due to lactose in the formulation obstructing equipment. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
